key_insight: SAMA factorizes instruction-guided video editing into two complementary components—Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment—allowing precise, instruction-driven semantic changes while faithfully preserving original motion without heavy reliance on external priors.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between making accurate semantic edits per instruction and maintaining temporal/motion fidelity in videos, avoiding brittle dependence on external priors (e.g., VLM features or structural conditions) that hurt robustness and generalization.
method: Factorization: split editing into Semantic Anchoring (localize and constrain semantic changes) and Motion Alignment (preserve temporal dynamics and frame-to-frame consistency).
Integrated training/architecture that minimizes explicit external priors and instead uses internal alignment mechanisms to balance edit precision and motion preservation.
Lightweight modules designed to plug into instruction-guided video editing pipelines, improving robustness and generalization across diverse instructions and motion patterns.
impact: Enables more reliable, generalizable instruction-guided video editing that produces faithful motion-preserving results—useful for content creation, VFX, AR/VR, and any application needing accurate, temporally consistent edits from natural-language instructions.
visual_elements: Before / After frame pair annotated with the instruction and highlighted semantic change regions.
Pipeline diagram showing the two-stage factorization: Semantic Anchoring → Motion Alignment, with data flow and module interactions.
Motion-consistency overlay (optical-flow arrows or frame-difference heatmap) comparing baseline vs SAMA to illustrate preserved motion.
Bar/line chart comparing semantic edit accuracy and temporal consistency metrics across SAMA and representative baselines.
paper_title: SAMA: Factorized Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
paper_authors: Xinyao Zhang, Wenkai Dong, Yuxin Song, Bo Fang, Qi Zhang
